rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wealthy guardian should abstain entirely from the orphan’s property; a poor guardian who manages it may take only customary compensation for his work.
rows.anchor: أي يطلب العفة ويوجدها ويظهرها عن الأكل منها جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor guardian’s customary allowance is proportionate to the wage earned through his effort.
rows.anchor: فقال معبرا بالأكل لأنه معظم المقصود : { فليأكل بالمعروف } أي بقدر أجرة سعيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardians must document the return of an orphan’s property because maturity and sound judgment vary, and witnesses prevent disputes and protect both sides.
rows.anchor: لأن الأحوال تتبدل , والرشد يتفاوت , فالإشهاد أقطع للشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Requiring witnesses deters a guardian from betrayal, since he knows a later claim will require evidence.
rows.anchor: والأمر بالإشهاد أزجر للولي عن الخيانة , لأن من عرف أنه لا يقبل عند الخصام إلا ببينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is a meticulous accountant; the closing warning cautions guardians and orphans against betrayal, transgression, and coveting another’s rights.
rows.anchor: أي محاسبا بليغا في الحساب , فهو أبلغ تحذيرا لهم وللأيتام من الخيانة والتعدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deny meeting God lose every reward they might have secured, and their denial continues until the Hour arrives.
rows.anchor: قد خسروا كل شيء يمكن إحرازه من الثواب العظيم واستمر تكذيبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour includes death as its beginning, since everyone who dies has reached his own Hour.
rows.anchor: وكذا الموت الذي هو مبدأها فإن من مات جاءت ساعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its arrival is sudden: people cannot know the precise time it will come, even in a general way.
rows.anchor: أو بغتتهم بإتيانها على حين غفلة , لا يمكن أن يشعروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling on regret as if summoning a companion is a metaphor that magnifies their remorse and warns people to avoid its causes.
rows.anchor: أي تعالى احضرينا أيها الحسرة اللائقة بنا في هذا المقام !

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their regret is for neglecting what would benefit them in the afterlife: disciplining the soul and following the messengers.
rows.anchor: ففاتنا ما يسعد فيها من تهذيب الأخلاق المهيئة للسباق بترك اتباع الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave people outward senses and bodily faculties, inward reason and thought, and prophets with miracles so they could acquire lasting knowledge and virtue; they squandered these tools on fleeting pleasures.
rows.anchor: وأفاض عليه نعما ظاهرة وهي الحواس الظاهرة المدركة والأعضاء والآلات الجثمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinners carry their sins as heavy loads on their backs; their deeds may be embodied as burdens, and the image conveys a horror beyond human comprehension.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يجسد أعمالهم أجسادا ثقالا , فيكلفوا حملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic rebuke gathers up the many defects of this burden and its unbearable weight.
rows.anchor: ألا ساء ما يزرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the wretched, worldly life is merely play and amusement; play is unlawful, fleeting activity that pleases the self, while amusement draws the self toward heedlessness.
rows.anchor: أي للأشقياء , وللحياة الدنيا شر للذين يلعبون , واللهو ما من شأنه أن يعجب النفس كالغناء والزينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Play precedes amusement because loss most often arises from play; when people tire of low distractions, they stir their desires with amusements.
rows.anchor: ولما كان السياق للخسارة , وكانت أكثر ما تكون من اللعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world is only a short period of play, and a sensible player regrets missing lasting gains once he sees what serious people achieved.
rows.anchor: فحينئذ ما هي إلا ساعة لعب , يندم الإنسان على ما فرط فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is better for those who cultivate taqwa, understood as fear of God that leads to obedience and abandoning sin, protecting them from divine anger.
rows.anchor: وهي الخوف من الله الذي يحمل على فعل الطاعات وترك المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses rhetorical omission: the worldly life’s outcome for its people is left implicit because the afterlife’s fruit makes it clear, and the afterlife’s state is likewise implied by the worldly contrast.
rows.anchor: فذكر حال الدنيا وحذف نتيجتها لأهلها لدلالة ثمرة الآخرة عليه وحذف ذكر حال الآخرة لدلالة ذكر حال الدنيا عليه , فهو احتباك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason should lead people to choose the lasting good over the transient one, so their preference for the perishing world prompts the rebuke, “Will you not reason?”
rows.anchor: ولما كان من شأن العقلاء الإقبال على الخير وترك غيره , تسبب عن إقبالهم على الفاني وتركهم الباقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s present-tense knowing denotes renewed knowledge of the opponents’ changing statements, not knowledge limited to the past; the Prophet should not grieve because God knows his hurt and rewards obedience.
rows.anchor: وعدل عن الماضي لئلا يظن الاختصاص به , فالمراد تحقق التجدد لتعلق العلم بتجدد الأقوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the celestial argument, Abraham openly disavows every form of associating partners with God, since the sun is the greatest and brightest visible celestial body.
rows.anchor: فلما أبطل بذلك جميع مذهبهم أظهر التوجه إلى الإله الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning his face to the Creator signifies wholly sincere devotion, as one who submits to something turns his face toward it.
rows.anchor: أي أخلصت قصدي غير معرج على شيء أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says “for the One who created” rather than “toward” the heavens and earth’s Creator to avoid suggesting that God occupies a place.
rows.anchor: وعبر باللام دون إلى لئلا يوهم الحيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanif means gently and naturally inclining with evidence, like the original human disposition, rather than rigidly imitating tradition.
rows.anchor: ميل مع الدليل سهولة ولطافة على ما هو دأب الفطرة الأولى التي فطر الله الناس عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s disavowal identifies him as outside the idolaters’ ranks and expresses a general rejection of anything resembling their associationism.
rows.anchor: أي لا أعد في عدادكم بشيء أقاربكم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s people argued that they would keep worshipping their inherited idols and threatened him with calamity if he did not stop opposing them.
rows.anchor: بأنهم لا ينفكون عن عبا تها لأنهم وجدوا آباءهم كذلك , وأنه إن لم يرجع عن الكلام فيها أصابته ببعض النوازل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their challenge is especially feeble after the clear proofs; the narrative leaves their arguments unstated as unworthy of mention and highlights Abraham’s answer.
rows.anchor: نزه المقام عن ذكرها , إشارة إلى أنها بحيث لا يستحق الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham says he hopes in and fears God, who alone is able to cause benefit or harm.
rows.anchor: فأنا أرجوه وأخافه لأنه قادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He denies fearing the idols because they are powerless; this implies that God alone can cause harm, and the argument reverses what the idolaters fear.
rows.anchor: ولا أرجوه لهداية ولا إضلال ولا غيرهما لأنه عاجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast is an instance of rhetorical ellipsis: God’s power to guide implies His power to misguide, while the idols’ inability to harm implies their inability to benefit.
rows.anchor: فأثبت لله القدرة بالهداية لأنها أشرف , وطوى الإضلال لدلالتها ودلالة ما نفي في جانب الشركاء عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s qualification “unless my Lord wills something” is no expression of doubt: only God knows hidden outcomes, and He can empower even an otherwise powerless being if He wills.
rows.anchor: فأنا لا أخاف في الحقيقة غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s encompassing knowledge entails power to remove every impediment if He chooses to empower the powerless; Abraham withholds certainty only because outcomes belong to God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: فهو إذا أراد إقدار العاجز أزال عنه كل مانع من القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Will you not remember?” calls them back to their inborn capacity to distinguish truth: idols cannot help or harm and are themselves manufactured.
rows.anchor: أي يقع منكم تذكر , فتميزوا بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham contrasts his lack of fear of powerless idols with their failure to fear God, who has power to punish them.
rows.anchor: وتعجب منهم في ظنهم خوفه من معبوداتهم بقوله منكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their idols have no revealed warrant that would shield them from God’s anger; mentioning and fronting “upon you” underscores the gravity of this foundational question.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المقام صعبا لأنه أصل الدين , أثبت الجار والمجرور وقدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham explains that idols cannot harm, while this passage identifies fear of harm from them as the danger being denied.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المحذور المنفي هنا إنما هو خوف الضرر من آلهتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham invokes God as Lord because the danger concerned harm and protection; Shuʿayb invokes the all-comprehensive divine name because the issue was returning to unbelief.
rows.anchor: اقتصر الخليل عليه السلام على صفة الربوبية المقتضية للرأفة والرحمة والكفاية والحماية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two prophets’ conditional language comes from one source, as does the reminder not to claim certainty about tomorrow without God’s will.
rows.anchor: من مشكاة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Which of the two parties” generalizes beyond Abraham and his people to God’s party and the idolaters’ party, compelling the audience to answer who deserves security.
rows.anchor: أي إن كان لكم علم فأخبروني عما سألتكم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe and do not mix faith with shirk alone receive security and guidance; the idolaters are astray and face ruin.
rows.anchor: أي وأنتم ضالون , فأنتم هالكون لإشرافكم على المهالك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet interpreted the unrestricted “injustice” as shirk, citing the description of shirk as a grave injustice; this reassured the Companions.
rows.anchor: وتفسير النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما أخرج الشيخان والترمذي والنسائي عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه لهذا الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the passage warns against shirk, “injustice” ultimately means mixing faith with no amount of shirk; the tanwin can suggest both greatness and smallness, making the wording encompass every degree.
rows.anchor: فالتنوين حينئذ للتحقير كما هو للتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After exposing the false foundations of the polytheists’ prohibitions, the verse announces the true religion: only the Creator and sovereign may declare what is forbidden.
rows.anchor: فليس التحريم لأحد غيره

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: “Come” calls listeners upward from ignorance and imitation to knowledge and good conduct; al-Zamakhshari says this once-special expression became common, even for a lower-status speaker addressing a superior.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب الكشاف : هو من الخاص الذي صار عاما , يعني حتى صار يقوله الأسفل للأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author glosses “I recite” as reading, from the root of recitation in which letters follow one another.
rows.anchor: من التلاوة وهي اتباع بعض الحروف بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibitions are put first because they matter most, and the verse begins with exclusive worship: removing vice precedes acquiring virtue.
rows.anchor: وكان المحرم أهم , قدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is paired with kindness to parents as gratitude to benefactors; killing children follows as the gravest wrong after shirk, beginning with the especially heinous motive of fearing poverty.
rows.anchor: وقرن به البر لأنهما من باب شكر المنعم وتعظيما لأمر العقوق , ثم أولاه القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names God’s provision for the already poor parents first, then for their children, because the killing is driven by present poverty.
rows.anchor: بالخطاب , أي أيها الفقراء , ثم عطف عليه الأبناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s commands also prohibit their opposites, so kindness is doubly reinforced by both an explicit command and an implicit ban on mistreatment.
rows.anchor: وكذا جميع المأمورات ساقها هذا السياق المفهم لأن أضدادها منهي عنها

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Unlike this verse’s present-poverty wording, 17:31 describes parents who fear future poverty despite current means; Abu Hayyan notes that 17:31 therefore names the children’s provision first.
rows.anchor: أن الآباء موسرون ولكنهم يخشون من إطعام الأبناء الفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on approaching grave indecencies is stronger than merely banning their commission, and “open or hidden” makes it comprehensive.
rows.anchor: وعظم أمرها بالنهي عن القربان فضلا عن الغشيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general ban on indecencies is followed by a specific prohibition of unlawful killing, with the exception restricted to an unmistakable, fully justified legal ground.
rows.anchor: أي الملك الأعلى عليكم قتلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Child-killing is forbidden three times in the passage; the closing “He has charged you” names these commands and prohibitions’ opposites as divine counsel, reinforced so people may reason.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت هذه الأشياء شديدة على النفس , ختمها بما لا يقوله إلا المحب الشفوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because property sustains life, the verse begins its next set of rules with wealth and singles out the vulnerable orphan’s property; even approaching it is prohibited except to improve and grow it.
rows.anchor: ولما كان أعظمها خطرا وحرمة مال اليتيم لضعفه وقلة ناصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardians may manage the orphan’s property only in the best way, such as developing and investing it, until the child reaches customary maturity and discernment.
rows.anchor: وهو سن يبلغ به أوان حصول عقله عادة وعقل يظهر به رشده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fair measure means full, equitable delivery without excess or shortfall; the qualification removes any implication that merely coming close is enough.
rows.anchor: أي إيفاء كائنا به من غير إفراط ولا تفريط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exact equality is often unattainable, so people owe sincere effort within their ability; anything beyond capacity is excused.
rows.anchor: أشار إلى أنه ليس على المكلف المبني أمره على العجز للضعف إلا الجهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When speaking in testimony, judgment, mediation, or any other matter, people must be just even about relatives, resisting affection, fear, or hopes of support.
rows.anchor: أي في شهادة أو في حكم أو توفيق بين اثنين أو غير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s covenant covers everything a person owes or is owed; the closing charge emphasizes remembering justice by judging for others as one would judge for oneself.
rows.anchor: وهذا يشمل كل ما على الإنسان وله , فإن الله لم يهمل شيئا بغير تقدم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use the opening waw with fath as a continuation; Ibn ʿAmir and Yaʿqub read it with kasra as the start of a new sentence.
rows.anchor: على قراءة الجماعة بالفتح , أي اتبعوه لذلك , وعلى قراءة ابن عامر ويعقوب بالكسر هو ابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path should be followed with full effort because it gathers people on truth and good, while paths branching from desire divide them.
rows.anchor: أي بغاية جهدكم لأنه الجامع للعباد على الحق الذي فيه كل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links this straight path to the earlier description of the Lord’s path and signs made clear for those who remember.
rows.anchor: وهذا كما مدحه سبحانه سابقا في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rulings are distributed across three verses, each ending with “He has charged you,” strengthening the instruction and inviting acceptance.
rows.anchor: وفصل ما هنا من الأحكام في ثلاث آيات , وختم كل آية لذلك بالوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing appeals progress from reason to remembrance to taqwa: reason calls for reflection, which leads to precaution against straying and ruin.
rows.anchor: لأنه إذا كان العقل دعا إلى التذكير فحمل على التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ sign established real truth by swallowing their objects, whereas the magicians’ craft was illusion; what they seemed to do had no reality beneath its appearance.
rows.anchor: باطن الأمر مطابق لما ظهر منه من ابتلاعها لأمتعتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “they used to do” with a past particle and imperfect verb suggests that, despite the craft they had mastered, their work was erased as an act.
rows.anchor: فدل بكان والمضارع على أنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians were defeated at the decisive event and returned humiliated, after imagining themselves and their supporters superior.
rows.anchor: جزاء على قلبهم لتلك الحقائق عن وجوهها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recognizing Moses’ act as a heavenly sign confirming his mission, the magicians fell prostrate from fear of God and longing to submit; God’s act through them was meant to bewilder Pharaoh and his people.
rows.anchor: ألقاهم ملقى الخوف من الله والشوق إلى الخضوع بين يديه والذل لديه حين عرفوا أن ما فعله موسى عليه السلام أمر سماوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prostration was a sign of complete submission and gratitude, and their immediate response led many of them to eternal felicity.
rows.anchor: شكرا لله تعالى وانسلاخا عن الكفر ودليلا على أقصى غايات الخضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They specify “Lord of Moses and Aaron” to prevent Pharaoh from claiming that he was the lord who raised Moses in his household.
rows.anchor: ثم أزالو الشبهة بحدذافيرها - لأن فرعون ربما ادعى بتربية موسى عليه السلام أنه المراد - بقولهم : { وهارون * }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode shows that witnessing a sign obliges belief for the person who sees it, even if the messenger was not sent specifically to that observer.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دليل على أن ظهور الآية موجب للإيمان عند ظهرت له , ولو أن الرسول غير مرسل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s question about believing before permission attempts to control the others’ response; he then falsely recasts their conviction as a prearranged plot to drive the Egyptians out.
rows.anchor: شرع في تهديدهم على وجه يمكر فيه بقومه ويلبس عليهم إيقافا لهم عن المبادرة إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh threatens opposite-side amputation, then crucifixion; the delayed “then” lengthens the threat to frighten the magicians and wavering onlookers, and crucifixion may mean a cross-shaped display or torture until bodily fluid runs.
rows.anchor: ولما كان مقصود هذه السورة الإنذار , فذكر فيها ما وقع لموسى عليه السلام والسحرة على وجه يهول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians accept that death is unavoidable whether Pharaoh crucifies them or spares them, so they are not concerned with remaining in worldly life.
rows.anchor: بالموت انقلابا ثابتا لا انفكاك لنا عنه إن صلبتنا أو تركتنا , لا طمع لنا في البقاء في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may also mean that execution will return them to the One who will take vengeance on Pharaoh for them.
rows.anchor: أو المراد أنا ننقلب إذا قتلنا إلى من يحسن إلينا بما منه الانتقام منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The only grievance Pharaoh has against them is their faith in God’s signs, which came from their benefactor and therefore called for gratitude, not punishment.
rows.anchor: أي فعلك ذلك بنا وتعيب علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not delay once the proof of truth arrived; that prompt recognition should earn honor rather than vengeance.
rows.anchor: أي حين { جاءتنا } لم نتأخر عن معرفة الصدق المصدق , وهذا يوجب الإكرام لا الانتقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They pray for encompassing patience under the threat and to have their souls taken while fully and inwardly submitted to the truth.
rows.anchor: أي اقبض أرواحنا وافية حال كوننا { مسلمين * }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God apparently answered their prayer, alluded to through their address to Him as Lord, by not empowering Pharaoh to carry out the threat.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الله تعالى أجابهم فيما سألوه تلويحا بذكر الرب فلم يقدره عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the general restrictions on associating with hostile polytheists, the verse establishes a limited middle course for any polytheist seeking protection after the truce period.
rows.anchor: عطف على ذلك طريقا آخر وسطا مقيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grant the seeker asylum and protection from anyone who might harm him while he listens to God’s recitation and learns its message.
rows.anchor: أي فآمنه ودافع عنه من يقصده بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If he remains a non-Muslim and wishes to leave, escort him to a secure place; fighting may resume only once he has safely arrived, without betrayal.
rows.anchor: ثم قاتله بعد بلوغه المأمن إن شئت من غير غدر ولا خيانه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says this rule remains operative and clear through the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : هي محكمة إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asylum is granted because these people lack knowledge: they have had no prior contact with prophethood, revelation, or scripture, and learning may benefit them.
rows.anchor: لا عهد لهم بنبوة ولا رسالة ولا كتاب , فإذا علموا أوشك أن ينفعهم العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception for those who kept their treaty refers back to the opening declaration about the polytheists who had made agreements, including the pact at al-Hudaybiyya.
rows.anchor: من { الذين } في قوله { براءة من الله ورسوله إلى الذين عاهدتم من المشركين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the dreadful scene of judgment, every obedient or disobedient soul encounters its prior deeds and learns whether they led to felicity or misery.
rows.anchor: اي تخبر وتخالط مميلة محلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive “they are returned” heightens fear: all are brought back through resurrection to God, with no ability to turn elsewhere or retain hope in their former false gods.
rows.anchor: أي بالبعث بالإحياء كما كانوا أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged partners are exposed as powerless creatures under God’s control, while God alone is the true master and protector.
rows.anchor: شركاءهم مربوبون مقهورون , لا قدرة لهم إلا على ما يقدرهم الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author defines “straying” as separation from one’s place, deriving the word from the yāʾ root rather than wāw; he also defines sufficiency, precedence, return, and mastership.
rows.anchor: والتنزيل : تفريق يزول به كل واحد عن مكانه , وهو من تفريق الجثث , وليس من الواوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions about provision, senses, life, death, and universal governance expose what the polytheists already admit, thereby proving God’s exclusive divinity and rebuking their denial of resurrection.
rows.anchor: فوبخهم بأن وجه السؤال إليهم عما هم معترفون بأنه مختص به ويدل قطعا على تفرده بجميع الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides rain and other benefits from the sky, and plants and other means of life from the earth.
rows.anchor: أي يجلب لكم الخيرات ايها المنكرون للبعث المدعون للشركة { من السمآء } أي بالمطر وغيره من المنافع { والأرض } بالنبات وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing is singular because most people share it equally, while eyes are plural; sight and hearing sustain bodily life and knowledge sustains spiritual life.
rows.anchor: ووحده للتساوي فيه في الغالب { والأبصار } التي تبصرون بها ما أنعم عليكم به في خلقها

rows.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Ali marvels that God made people see through fat, hear through bone, and speak through flesh.
rows.anchor: قال : سبحانه من بصر بشحم , وأسمع بعظم , وأنطق بلحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioning moves from the obvious gifts people experience to the prior origin of creation: living beings emerge from dead matter and dead matter from living beings.
rows.anchor: نبههم على ما قبله من بدء الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The life/death contrast covers animals and plants as well as a sperm drop and its products, moving from deficiency to completion.
rows.anchor: من الحيوان والنبات { من الميت } أي من النطفة ونحوها { ويخرج الميت } أي من النطفة ونحوها مما لا ينمو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final question about managing all affairs summarizes God’s comprehensive governance; the polytheists acknowledge that God alone does this.
rows.anchor: ومن يدبر الأمر } أي كله التدبير العام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their admission that God alone provides and governs makes their failure to guard themselves from His punishment incoherent, since they associate partners in divinity.
rows.anchor: أي تجعلون وقاية بينكم وبين عقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God whose unique power and actions were listed is the true Lord; true lordship requires all those attributes, which none other possesses.
rows.anchor: أي الثابته ربوبيته ثباتا لا ريب فيه لاجتماع الصفات الماضية له لا لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no middle position after truth except misguidance, so no rational person should turn from truth to error.
rows.anchor: فغنه لا واسطة بينهما - بما أنبأ عنه إسقاط الجار , ولا يعدل عاقل عن الحق إلى الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s decree is fulfilled against those who leave obedience and the true religion and do not believe; “they were one community” refers to humanity’s original unity in Adam’s religion.
rows.anchor: أي أوقعوا الترك لأمر الله وأوجدوا عصيانه وفعلوا الخروج عن طريق الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On another reading of the passage’s logic, God’s unique rule over provision, creation, and governance proves exclusive divinity: a rival equal in power could resist Him, which is impossible.
rows.anchor: لأنه لو كان قادر يساويه في مقدوره لأمكن أن يمانعه , وبطل أن يكون قادرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those far from mercy cannot frustrate God anywhere on earth, because their inability to escape His will extends across all possible circumstances.
rows.anchor: عجزهم بأنهم لا يقدرون على بلوغ العالم العلوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have no protectors besides God to manage their interests or shield them from calamity; one unable to escape God alive cannot do so after death.
rows.anchor: أي يفعلون معهم ما يفعل القريب من تولي المصالح والحماية من المصائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment is doubled because they multiplied their sins; the passive construction emphasizes the fact of doubling itself.
rows.anchor: { يضاعف } أي يفعل يه فعل من يناظر آخر في الزيادة , وبناه للمفعول لأنالمرجع وجود المضاعفة مطلقا { لهم العذاب } اي لما كانوا يضاعفون المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their failure to hear or see is figurative: passion and corrupt dispositions make them reject truth as though they could not bear their senses; the lack of ability deepens the blame.
rows.anchor: وهو كناية عن عدم قبولهم للحق وأن شدة إعراضهم عنه وصلت إلى حد صارت فيه توصغ بعد الاستطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the wording can be read as rhetorical ellipsis: denial of ability in one sense implies it in the other, and denial of seeing implies denial of hearing.
rows.anchor: ونفي الإبصار يدل على نفي السمع أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lose themselves by wasting the original disposition that readily follows good and resists evil.
rows.anchor: اي بتضييع الفطرة الأولى التي هي سهولة الانقياد للخير وصعوبة الانقياد للشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their invented gods disappear and cannot help them; whoever loses himself through claiming a partnership with his Creator is among the most lost.
rows.anchor: أي يتعمدون كذبه مما ادعوا كونهم آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No doubt” identifies these afterlife deniers as the most lost of all, with the repeated pronoun and “they” giving the superlative emphasis.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المقام جديرا بالمبالغة في وصفهم بالخسارة , أعاد الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author defines inability to thwart as being unable to prevent what God wills, doubling as an increase by an equal or larger amount, and capacity as a power by which limbs act.
rows.anchor: والإعجاز : الامتناع من المراد بما لا يمكن معه إيقاعه ؛ والمضاعفة : الزيادة على المقدار بمثله أو أكثر ؛ والاستطاعة : قوة ينطاع بها الجوارح للفعل

rows.speaker: الرضي والسفاقسي
rows.claim: Al-Radi and al-Saqafsi report several grammatical accounts of “la jarama”: “la” may reject prior speech or be extra because the phrase carries an oath, while Sibawayhi and al-Khalil treat the expression as a compound past verb meaning “it is certain.”
rows.anchor: قالالرضي في شرح الحاجبية والبرهان السفاقسي في إعرابه ما حاصله : والغالب بعد { لا جرم } الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other grammarians say “jarama” means “is true,” making it the noun of “la” with “they” as predicate; al-Kisaʾi explains the phrase as “no denial or prevention.”
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي معناها : لا صد ولا منع

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj treats the phrase as uncombined: “la” denies the claim that idols help, “jarama” means “earned,” and “they” is its object.
rows.anchor: وعن الزجاج أنها غير مركبة , ولا نفي لما قيل من أن لهم أصناما تنفعهم

rows.speaker: الفراهي
rows.claim: Al-Farahi derives the expression from an original sense of “inevitably” or “there is no alternative,” with the root referring to cutting, and explains the phrase’s oath-like use.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراهي : كلمة كانت في الأصل بمعنى لا بد ولا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers understanding the root through the recurrent idea of disturbance: in the mind, reflection unsettles an opinion and opens what was closed, while related forms express doubt, confusion, sin, mixture, or separation.
rows.anchor: وقد علم من هذا أن جميع تصاريف المادة تدور على الاضطراب وهو بين في غير العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this analysis, “la jarama” means there is no uncertainty or wavering that they will be punished; in context, denying doubt affirms certainty.
rows.anchor: ظهر أن معنى ( لا جرم ) أنهم لا ظن ولا اضطراب في أنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This also explains Sibawayhi’s gloss “it is true”: “la” negates the opposite of the assertion, so the phrase confirms that their fate is established and every contrary is excluded.
rows.anchor: فكأنه قيل : حق وثبت أنهم كذا وانتفى كل ما يضاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author treats “la” as an emphatic particle of negation in this expression, comparable to the emphatic force of “innama.”
rows.anchor: فهي نافية لضد ما دخلت عليه , فكأنه قيل : حق وثبت أنهم كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥ after “la jarama,” the construction looks to its original “there is no alternative that…” form; kasra reflects its later oath-like force, as in “I swear that you are standing.”
rows.anchor: فمن فتح فللنظر إلى أصل { لا جرم } كما نقول : لا بد أن نفعل كذا
